title: bug: gemini mode silently falls back to the Gemini CLI with Antigravity's flags when agy is missing (moe-agent.sh about :11612-11617, moe-agent.ps1 about :10993-11003), and agentCommand 'agy' is not recognized as gemini mode (moe-agent.sh :639): port PR #208's Antigravity-only gemini mode (MOE_AGY_COMMAND, one fixed not-found error, parity needles, docs and labels) to the work branch so #208 can close
description:
Filed by the governor (governor-e6142a94) on 2026-11-04. The human left the decision on PR #208 to the governor ("as u decide"), and the decision is to port it.

PROBLEM, on moe/work-2026-10-24, the same as main since 3272b871 ("feat: use Antigravity (agy) for gemini agent mode", 2026-09-29):
- moe-agent.sh about :11612-11617, and moe-agent.ps1 about :10993-11003: when agentCommand is `gemini`, the launcher switches to `agy` only if agy is on PATH.
- Otherwise it keeps `gemini` and runs the Gemini CLI with the agy-mode argv. The Gemini CLI rejects agy's flags, so the seat fails confusingly instead of saying Antigravity is missing.
- The not-found message ("Antigravity command not found: <cmd>") names whichever binary is missing, which may be `gemini`.
- moe-agent.sh :639 maps only `gemini` to the gemini cliType, so `agentCommand: "agy"` is not recognized at all.

FIX: PR #208 (fix/agy-bom-flake, commit "fix(wrapper): restore ps1 UTF-8 BOM, run Antigravity only in gemini mode"). Read it with `gh.exe pr diff 208` and `gh.exe pr view 208` (WSL has only gh.exe). Re-apply its intent to the CURRENT files by anchor, never by line. The PR is against 09-29 main and conflicts.
1. Both launchers. Gemini mode always runs Antigravity:
   - take the binary from `MOE_AGY_COMMAND`, else `agy` on PATH;
   - never fall back to the Gemini CLI;
   - map both `gemini` and `agy` to the gemini cliType;
   - with no agy, stop with ONE fixed message in both launchers: 'Antigravity CLI (agy) not found: <cmd>. Install Antigravity, or set MOE_AGY_COMMAND to the agy binary path' (take the exact strings from #208).
2. scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1: require the shared literals (MOE_AGY_COMMAND and the not-found message), as #208's parity hunk does.
3. Docs and labels, as in #208:
   - README.md: the CLI list names Antigravity (agy);
   - docs/CONFIGURATION.md: the `MOE_AGY_COMMAND` row, and `agentCommand` gemini "runs Antigravity agy";
   - docs/GETTING_STARTED.md: sign-in with `agy`;
   - docs/SCHEMA.md: the 'GEMINI' comment;
   - JetBrains: TerminalAgentLauncher.kt `GEMINI("Antigravity", "gemini")` and MoeBundle.properties `moe.panel.provider.gemini=Antigravity`.
   JetBrains is first. If moe-vscode shows a provider label for gemini, give it parity in the same row; otherwise say none exists.
4. A test pins the behaviour on both engines with fake binaries. No real agy or gemini is needed: gemini plus a fake agy runs the fake agy, and gemini with no agy stops with the message and never runs a fake `gemini`.

ALREADY ON THE BRANCH. Skip these parts of #208:
- the ps1 UTF-8 BOM, which CLAUDE.md requires and parity-check enforces;
- the heartbeatStop.test.ts flake, which the work branch fixed differently with `PWSH_CASE = { retry: 2, timeout: 15000 }`.

ORDER. dependsOn CQ-M07t (task-527735ea), which edits both launchers. task-e444f6ae also edits moe-agent.ps1 after t, in the check-dispatch stop area, far from the gemini launch block. Serialize the two with an edge if your plan touches nearby code; otherwise say why parallel is safe.
No change to the CQ-M07 turn-on row: gemini mode is outside the verified-local acceptance.

CLOSE-OUT. When this row is DONE, the governor closes PR #208 as superseded, with a comment naming this row and its commit. Never close it from this row.
definitionOfDone: Both launchers run agy for agentCommand gemini or agy (from MOE_AGY_COMMAND, else PATH) and never the Gemini CLI. With no agy, both stop with the same fixed not-found message naming MOE_AGY_COMMAND. A fake-binary test pins this on bash and on both PowerShell engines.

parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 require the shared literals. README, CONFIGURATION, GETTING_STARTED, SCHEMA and the JetBrains provider label say gemini mode runs Antigravity (agy), with VS Code parity if it shows a label. The plan's verification passes fresh.

comments.author: architect-2a219562
comments.content:
Verification trap, found by architect-2a219562 while planning task-ff0df867 (proof run in bash). Step 6 runs the 5 checkRefs "joined with ' && '", but each ref is a `;`-sequence. `&&` therefore links only one ref's last command to the next ref's first command (its `cd`). Refs 0, 1 and 4 also end in `exit $f`/`exit $r`, so a joined run exits 0 right after "docs check A f=0" and checks B to E never run. Proof: `bash -c 'echo "check A f=0"; f=0; exit $f && echo B1; echo "check B ran"; false'` prints only the first line and returns 0.
Fix, with no ref byte changed: wrap each ref in a subshell, `( <ref0> ) && ( <ref1> ) && ( <ref2> ) && ( <ref3> ) && ( <ref4> )`. Each `exit` then ends only its own subshell, and the chain stops at the first red ref with that ref's code. task-c199e177 has the same trap without the exit (see the comment there). @governor-e6142a94 FYI, in case you want to amend the step text.
